newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Suspected bubonic plague kills 30 people in Zambia.
newsitem.headline: Suspected bubonic plague kills 30 people in Zambia.

text.p: Suspected bubonic plague has killed 30 people in southern Zambia in the past month, the state Zambia Information Service (ZIS) said on Monday.
"The bubonic pneumonia plague death toll in Namwala has risen to 30 following five more deaths at the weekend," it said.
At least 60 more people were being treated for the plague at health centres in the Namwala agricultural district, ZIS said, quoting nurses and doctors at the clinics.
Health ministry officials in Lusaka confirmed the deaths but said there was no conclusive evidence that the epidemic was bubonic plague.
"Investigations to establish the nature of the outbreak are still being conducted," a ministry official told Reuters.
Bubonic plague, transmitted by fleas which live on rats, can kill within 48 hours if not treated. Symptoms include high fever, chills and headaches.
